facts.claim: In document authoring, a block is a table whose first (header) row carries the block name; the content model is the row/cell structure authors fill in beneath it.

facts.claim: Block variants are authored in parentheses after the block name in the header row (e.g. 'Hero (Dark)') and become extra CSS classes on the block element; comma-separated options become separate classes, multi-word options are hyphenated.

facts.claim: An embed block with a <picture> next to the video link uses the image as a click-to-play placeholder; without an image it lazy-loads the iframe when scrolled into view. The 'embed-youtube' class is added by embed.js at decoration, not by auto-blocking.

facts.claim: EDS does not support nested blocks (no table inside a block table); content allows only one level: a section contains default content and blocks.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/markup-sections-blocks ('Sections can contain multiple blocks. Blocks should never be nested as it makes things very hard to use for authors.'); https://www.aem.live/developer/component-model-definitions ('deliberately allows only a single level of nesting, which is any default content or block contained by a section'); https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #2 'No nested blocks for authors'
facts.question: Can an author put a block inside a cell of another block in EDS? What nesting does the content model allow?

facts.claim: Container components that need to hold other blocks (tabs, accordions) are modeled as separate sections that auto-blocking combines into one block.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/component-model-definitions ('in order to have more complex visual components that can contain other components, they have to be modelled as sections and combined together using auto-blocking client side. Typical examples of this are tabs and collapsible sections like accordions')
facts.question: Given EDS's nesting limit, how does aem.live recommend building container components such as tabs or accordions whose panels contain other blocks?

facts.claim: Fragments - linking from a block to a separate document that holds the inner blocks - are an alternative to nesting blocks.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #2 ('Consider fragments (referencing other documents) or links (with auto blocking) to reduce the authoring complexity'); aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/scripts.js:L82-98 auto-loads links containing /fragments/ via blocks/fragment/fragment.js loadFragment
facts.question: Besides auto-blocking, what does aem.live suggest instead of nesting one block inside another, and how does the boilerplate pull such content in?

facts.claim: Fragments fit content reused across many pages (header/footer, sign-up form, legal disclaimer); they cost authors indirection (worse when nested), and SEO-relevant content belongs on the page itself.
facts.skillSays: Fragments: 'When the nested content is complex, reused across pages, or managed separately' (references/advanced-scenarios.md:66)
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #12 'Fragments may be harmful'
facts.question: What does aem.live's content-modeling guidance say about when fragments are appropriate and what they cost authors?

facts.claim: Authors should paste fully qualified URLs when referencing other content (fragments, pages, data); code extracts the pathname where needed.

facts.claim: A widget is a self-contained, application-like piece of functionality (forms, search results, product listings/indexes, filtering, dealer locators, sign-in/account, calculators) that authors reference by URL; it has no table to fill in and is not a block.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/widgets ('Widgets are the application parts of a website ... Typical examples are forms, product listing pages, search results, filtering and other indexes, dealer locators, sign-in and account management, and calculators ... There is no table to fill in')
facts.question: What is a 'widget' in AEM Edge Delivery Services and how does it differ from a block?

facts.claim: A widget lives in /widgets/<name>/ with <name>.html (markup/placeholders), <name>.css, <name>.js (a decorate function like a block) and an optional <name>.json for config/data.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/widgets ('/widgets/hello-world/hello-world.html ... .css ... .js ... .json (optional)')
facts.question: What files make up an EDS widget and where do they live in the project?

facts.claim: Authors place a widget by pasting a link to its .html file (e.g. https://main--repo--org.aem.page/widgets/hello-world/hello-world.html) alone in a paragraph; it is auto-blocked into a widget whose element gets a class matching the widget name.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/widgets ('When the link is the only thing in its paragraph, it is automatically turned into a widget block ... given a class matching the widget name'); aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/scripts.js:L53-74 buildWidgetAutoBlocks (any a[href*="/widgets/"]; replaces the paragraph if the link is its sole content, else just the link) and blocks/widget/widget.js
facts.question: How does an author place a widget on an EDS page, and how does it get turned into a component?

facts.claim: Widget parameters are passed as a query string on the widget URL; each parameter becomes a data-* attribute on the widget element (e.g. ?name=World -> data-name="World").
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/widgets ('Each parameter becomes a data- attribute on the widget element'); aem-boilerplate@5cea543 blocks/widget/widget.js applyWidgetShell (searchParams.forEach -> widget.dataset[key])
facts.question: How can an author pass settings to an EDS widget, and how does the widget code read them?

facts.claim: Choose a widget for application-like functionality used in one or a few places; choose a block for repeated, content-driven structures authors fill in across many pages.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/widgets 'When to use a widget' ('For repeated, content-driven structures that authors fill in across many pages, a block remains the right tool')
facts.question: When should an EDS developer build a widget rather than a block?

facts.claim: Putting content that is native default content (text, heading, image) into a block (e.g. a Text, Heading or Image block) is an anti-pattern; prefer default content wherever possible.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #1 ('It is definitely an anti-pattern to have things that are represented natively as default content and put them into a block, so something like a Text, Heading or Image block yields a bad authoring perspective')
facts.question: According to David's Model, what is wrong with creating a 'Text' or 'Heading' block?

facts.claim: Content models must not require authors to type HTML, CSS or JSON into documents.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #15 ('if you see tags <tag> or curly braces { } in a document you are looking most certainly at a content modeling mistake')
facts.question: What does David's Model say about HTML, CSS or JSON appearing in an authored document?

facts.claim: Don't hide extra semantics in image alt text (e.g. config or captions encoded in alt); authors can't easily see it and copy/paste may lose it.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/davidsmodel Rule #13 'Don't overload image alt-text semantics'
facts.question: What does David's Model say about storing extra information in image alt text?
